data.title: Cambi ASA (OB:CAMBI) Just Reported And Analysts Have Been Lifting Their Price Targets
data.description:
Shareholders might have noticed that Cambi ASA (OB:CAMBI) filed its second-quarter result this time last week. The early response was not positive, with shares down 3.0% to kr22.60 in the past week. Overall the results were a little better than the analysts were expecting, with revenues beating forecasts by 8.1%to hit kr265m. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Cambi's two analysts is for revenues of kr1.03b in 2026. This reflects a reasonable 7.3% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of kr1.03b and earnings per share (EPS) of kr0.70 in 2026. So we can see that while the consensus made no real change to its revenue estimates, it also no longer provides an earnings per share estimate. This suggests that revenues are what the market is focusing on after the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Cambi

The average price target rose 27% to kr28.00, with the analysts clearly having become more optimistic about Cambi'sprospects following these results.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Cambi's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2026 expected to display 15% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 19% over the past five years. Juxtapose this against the other companies in the industry with analyst coverage, which are forecast to grow their revenues (in aggregate) 11% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while Cambi's revenue growth is expected to slow, it's still expected to grow faster than the industry itself.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that the analysts reconfirmed their revenue estimates for next year, suggesting that the business is performing in line with expectations. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was also a nice increase in the price target, with the analysts clearly feeling that the intrinsic value of the business is improving.

We have estimates for Cambi from its two analysts out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

That said, it's still necessary to consider the ever-present spectre of investment risk. We've identified 1 warning sign with Cambi , and understanding it should be part of your investment process.

data.title: What Evergy (EVRG)'s Raised Earnings Guidance Means For Shareholders
data.description:
• Evergy reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$2,096.6 million and net income of US$612.9 million, raised full year adjusted earnings guidance to US$4.35 to US$4.50 per share, increased the quarterly dividend to US$0.7225 per share, and outlined a large scale data center expansion with Digital Realty.
  • The combination of higher earnings guidance, a 4% dividend uplift and a potential US$4 billion capital program with Digital Realty indicates that Evergy is focusing on large load growth while committing more cash returns to shareholders.
  • The next step is to examine how Evergy's raised earnings guidance, supported by expanding data center load, could influence the longer term investment narrative.

Evergy Investment Narrative Recap

For Evergy, the core view is that large data center and industrial demand, combined with heavy grid and generation investment, can support steady earnings while keeping regulators focused on customer bill impacts. The raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to US$4.35 to US$4.50 reflects that view. In the near term, the key swing factor remains execution on new large load contracts and the timing of their usage.

The biggest risk remains on the cost and funding side. Evergy plans high capital spending and already has interest coverage flagged as tight, with dividends not well covered by free cash flow. The latest results do not remove that concern, so the balance among growth spending, financing costs and bill affordability stays central for the next phase.

The most relevant update is the letter of intent with Digital Realty for a potential 1.4 GW project and roughly US$4 billion of capital investment. This is directly tied to Evergy’s data-center-led demand thesis and its plan to grow the regulated rate base through 2030 and beyond. The new agreements that add about 110 MW to existing large load contracts point in the same direction.

This opportunity comes with execution and regulatory risk. Building that much capacity requires Evergy to manage construction costs, interest expense and equity issuance while maintaining acceptable returns. At the same time, regulators will monitor customer affordability and reliability. For you as a shareholder, the key question is whether future earnings from those long-term electric service agreements will comfortably offset the additional capital expenditure and funding burden.

Evergy Forecasts and What Needs To Happen

Evergy's narrative projects US$7.3b revenue and US$1.3b earnings by 2029. This lines up with analysts assuming 6.4% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$374m from US$925.8m today.

data.title: What Investors Overlooked Before Grupo Casas Bahia Fell 79%
data.description:
When Grupo Casas Bahia released its Q2 2026 update showing R$6,977 million in revenue alongside a net loss of R$10,117 million, the numbers framed a stark year for holders. Holding Grupo Casas Bahia over the past year would have meant a 78.5% loss, including dividends. If you had put money in on 6 November 2025, how should this outcome reshape expectations about whether the digitalization story can offset legacy store pressures?

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

If the move has made Grupo Casas Bahia harder to judge, start where the gap is still open and scan 224 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Two Stories Investors Were Choosing Between On Grupo Casas Bahia

The shares cost R$3.36 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Grupo Casas Bahia then had to decide which of two stories felt more credible.

The bullish narrative put Fair Value at R$7.96, anchored in a view that digitalization and Latin American demand would support revenue growth of 5.9% a year and lift profit margin to 6.2% within three years.

The bearish case set Fair Value at R$3, stressing that legacy stores and high fixed costs might keep pressure on profitability even if revenue rose 4.9% annually and margin only reached 6.0%.

What The Results Changed For The Grupo Casas Bahia Thesis

The Q2 2026 figures gave investors a hard reference point. Grupo Casas Bahia reported revenue of R$6,977 million compared with R$6,867 million in Q2 2025. However, the loss deepened from R$555 million to R$10,117 million and net margin moved from a loss of 8.1% to a loss of 145.0%. That combination challenged both the optimistic and cautious profitability paths.

The key lesson is simple. When any retailer sells more but sees the loss widen sharply, it is important to watch the net margin line as closely as the growth claim, then decide what you are really paying for.

What You Are Really Paying For In Grupo Casas Bahia Today

Grupo Casas Bahia now trades at R$0.71 after a 78.5% loss over the past year, and the selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits above that quote based on its own framework rather than any proven benchmark.

The Narrative leans on digital channels, credit products, and a reshaped balance sheet. A buyer today would need to believe that cost cuts and online scale can eventually turn current losses into sustained positive margins.

"Accelerated digital transformation, credit solutions expansion, and operational efficiencies are strengthening revenue growth, profitability, and market share. Improved capital structure and cost reductions are supporting growth initiatives, margin expansion, and stronger long-term financial stability."

One Narrative has put a figure on that disagreement. → See the Narrative with its higher Fair Value, assumptions and all

Another Digital Retail Angle

Grupo Casas Bahia shows how hard omnichannel retail can be when losses build. You might still like Latin American shoppers steadily moving online.

data.title: How Stronger Revenue Will Impact Con Edison (ED) Investors
data.description:
• Consolidated Edison reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$4.91b and net income of US$766m, with basic EPS from continuing operations at US$2.07, all above the prior year period.
  • The utility paired this higher year to date profit with plans for about US$797m of climate resilience spending through 2030, linking recent earnings strength to long term infrastructure hardening.
  • We will now look at how Consolidated Edison’s stronger revenue performance fits into its existing investment narrative and how it may influence that narrative over time.

Consolidated Edison Investment Narrative Recap

For a shareholder in Consolidated Edison, the core belief is that a tightly regulated utility can keep turning heavy grid and resilience spending into dependable earnings. The latest quarter delivered higher revenue and net income year on year, which supports that thesis. The near term swing factor is still how regulators treat returns on this growing rate base, and this update does not materially change that.

The biggest operational worry remains stress during extreme weather and the cost of preventing or fixing outages. Higher nine month profit gives management some room to fund climate and reliability projects, but large capital needs, debt coverage and free cash flow pressure stay front of mind for anyone watching the balance sheet.

The most relevant recent announcement is Consolidated Edison’s plan for about US$797m of climate resilience investment from 2026 to 2030. That sits on top of a much larger long term grid program and directly links to the rate base growth many investors focus on. It also targets the same reliability issues that showed up during the 2026 heat waves.

This resilience plan interacts closely with the current earnings story. Stronger operating results in 2026 help support a heavier capital program, while regulators decide how much of that spending goes into rates and allowed returns. For you, the key question is whether this combination of higher capital intensity, debt funding needs and regulatory oversight still lines up with your view of Consolidated Edison’s risk and reward profile.

Analyst Expectations Behind the Consolidated Edison Story

Analysts are effectively sketching a steady, regulated glide path for Consolidated Edison. Their models assume revenue grows by 3.5% a year over the next few years while profit margins lift from 12.5% today to 14.2% by 2029. That set up points to earnings moving from about US$2.2b today to a consensus forecast of roughly US$2.8b by 2029, an increase of about US$600m that depends heavily on regulators allowing returns on a larger rate base.

Those same forecasts feed directly into how the stock is currently framed. To line up with the analyst view, you would need to accept that by 2029 Consolidated Edison generates about US$19.6b of revenue and US$2.8b of profit, with the shares trading around 18.9x those earnings. The implied future P/E sits a little below the current US integrated utilities industry level quoted in the report, which suggests the group of analysts see the stock as reasonably priced rather than a clear outlier on either value or risk.

Consolidated Edison's narrative projects about US$19.6b revenue and US$2.8b earnings by 2029. This requires 3.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of roughly US$600m from current earnings of about US$2.2b.
